result.title: TDLM: Adaptive Temporal Integration for Diffusion Language Models
result.summary: Masked diffusion language models repeatedly compute representations for unresolved tokens, but conventional denoisers do not explicitly retain these representations for reuse across steps. We introduce Temporal Self-Conditioning Diffusion Language Model (TDLM), which lets each unresolved position attend to its own history of hidden representations within a frozen denoiser. This gives later predictions access to computation already performed. Training uses self-generated trajectories and a simple cross-entropy objective for tokens revealed between consecutively sampled decoding steps, while causal temporal attention permits parallel evaluation during training. On LLaDA, the temporal modules add only approximately 0.84% trainable parameters. Across LLaDA and Dream, the main comparison shows up to 7.15$\times$ faster generation than the corresponding original diffusion language model, with competitive answer quality on the evaluated tasks. These results motivate temporal memory as a practical way to make more effective use of repeated denoising computation.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TDLM，在冻结的 diffusion LM denoiser 内让每个未解决位置通过因果时间注意力访问自身历史隐表示，使后续步骤能复用已算出的计算；训练用自生成轨迹加交叉熵，仅增加约 0.84% 参数，在 LLaDA 与 Dream 上取得最高 7.15 倍加速。
AI.relevance_reason: 跨步保留并更新隐状态、按轨迹段做监督的机制，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态的循环更新与训练期监督线索；但属纯文本扩散模型，状态是否真正承载任务必要内容及其与并行训练评估的对应关系仍需看原文核实。
